mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and positively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when UNRATE decreases, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts indicate strong demand in the housing market, which positively impacts the broader economy and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase but SPX returns are negative, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and payroll employment increases, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Both UNRATE and PAYEMS improve, but SPX returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates strong economic activity, which positively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production increases but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a low unemployment rate combined with high federal funds rate indicates tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE is low and FEDFUNDS are high, but SPX returns are positive more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales indicate strong consumer demand, which positively impacts S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales increase but SPX returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the consumer price index suggests inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI increases but SPX returns are positive more than 30% of the time.
